info.album: Honky Tonk Women / You Can't Always Get What You Want

podcast.body: Released in 1969, "Honky Tonk Woman" was the A-side to which "You Can't Always Get What You Want" was initially relegated as the B-side. "You can't always get what you want by the Rolling Stones began as a B side to Hunky Tonk woman in 1969."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Digital Debris Part 1: B-Sides and Bonus Tracks

podcast.body: This song reached the top 10 in the fall of 1969. Its lyrics, such as "I laid a Dave Orsay in New York City. I had to put up some kind of a fight. The lady then she covered me with roses. She blew my nose and then she blew my mind," were quite suggestive and contributed to a "battle of musical wills" on the charts with more innocent songs like "Sugar, Sugar." "The Stones had honky-talk women in the top 10 in the fall of 1969."

This song was at number one on the Billboard Hot 100 at the end of August 1969, only to be knocked off the top spot by The Archies' "Sugar Sugar." "Number one was honky talk women by the Rolling Stones. It took three weeks but sugar sugar by the Archies knocked honky talk women by one of the greatest rock bands of all time out of the number one spot and it stayed there for a month."

podcast.body: This song was performed by Rick Nelson at the 1971 Madison Square Garden concert, where he was booed for playing his new country rock material instead of his earlier hits. The audience strongly rejected hearing this type of song from him. "And they most definitely did not want to hear honky-talk women or traveling men."
